transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Hello, doctor. I came in because when I try to talk things through with people, my thoughts get all jumbled and I just can't seem to keep a straight line in a conversation anymore. It has been really worrying me and my daughter, so she helped me come see you today.

Did this confusion and trouble following a conversation come on suddenly over hours or days and change during the day, or has it been building up slowly over months? Have you also had any recent illness, fever, surgery, new medications, or alcohol/drug use around the time it started?

No, it didn't come on suddenly; it has been creeping in slowly for almost a year now, starting the year after my husband passed away. I haven't had any recent illnesses, fevers, surgeries, or new medications, and I don't drink or use drugs. It has just been a gradual change over these past months.
Besides conversations, have you been having trouble with day-to-day tasks like managing bills, taking medicines, cooking, or getting lost in familiar places? If so, when did that start?

Yes, I've really been struggling with my day-to-day tasks. I used to manage my own bills and help organize church dinners, but now my daughter has to come over every week to sort my mail and make sure I don't miss payments or appointments. These difficulties have been creeping in for almost a year now, starting the year after my husband passed away.

Have you been forgetting recent conversations or misplacing things more than before, even when someone reminds you? Or is the main problem more finding the right words and keeping your thoughts organized?

It's definitely more about keeping my thoughts organized than just forgetting things. When I try to talk, my thoughts get completely jumbled up and I'll start mixing up the electric bill, my husband's old toolbox, and choir songs all at once. I completely lose my train of thought, and it leaves the people I'm talking to looking very confused.

Have you also been having trouble understanding the meaning of words or recognizing familiar people or objects, even when you can see them clearly? Or is it mainly that your speech becomes jumbled while you still know what things and people are?

No, I don't have any trouble recognizing my friends or understanding what words mean. It's strictly that my thoughts get all jumbled when I try to talk, and I end up drifting off onto unrelated things like my husband's toolbox or the weather, even though I know exactly what those things are.

Along with the jumbled speech, have you or your family noticed major changes in your personality or behavior, like becoming socially inappropriate, losing empathy, acting impulsively, or developing new repetitive habits? Or has it mostly been the speech problem without those behavior changes?

Yes, there have been some strange changes in my behavior that embarrass me. Sometimes at church or the senior center, I will just freeze in place holding a dish or a songbook, or find myself flapping my hands and humming without even realizing it. I only notice something is wrong when people stare at me or gently take things out of my hands to guide me to a seat.
Have you ever been diagnosed with Huntington’s disease, or do you have a family history of it? Have you also noticed involuntary jerky movements or worsening coordination over time?
No, I have never been diagnosed with Huntington's disease, and I don't have any family history of it. I also haven't noticed any kind of involuntary jerky movements.

Have you ever been diagnosed with Parkinson’s disease or had symptoms like a resting tremor, slowness of movement, stiffness, or shuffling when you walk? If so, did those movement symptoms start before the thinking and speech problems?
No, I have never been diagnosed with Parkinson's disease. I also haven't had any symptoms like resting tremors, stiffness, or shuffling when I walk.

Have you been seeing things that others do not see, like people or animals, or having big ups and downs in your alertness and thinking from one time of day to another? If so, did those start around the same time as the speech and thinking problems?
No, I haven't seen anything that isn't really there, like people or animals. My alertness and thinking also stay pretty steady throughout the day without those kinds of ups and downs.

opening_question.question: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

final_diagnosis.reason: Progressive major neurocognitive decline with prominent disorganized/jumbled speech and executive dysfunction, preserved recognition/word meaning, associated behavioral stereotypies/freezing, and impaired instrumental daily functioning is most consistent with dementia in Pick's disease (frontotemporal dementia). Delirium is unlikely due to gradual onset and no fluctuation or medical trigger; Lewy body and Parkinson-related dementias are not supported by absent hallucinations, fluctuation, or parkinsonism; Huntington-related dementia is not supported by absent history/chorea.
